svg.title: Inside our tiny GPT: from text to the next token
svg.desc: A beginner guide to the tuned GPT. Text pieces become IDs; learned token and position vectors are added. Attention is causal: current and earlier positions only. Training changes the learned numbers; generation reuses them. Input-dependent activation vectors pass through six pre-norm transformer blocks, each containing attention and a feedforward multilayer perceptron, plus layer norms and residual connections. Final LayerNorm acts within each token vector, an untied head computes vocabulary scores, softmax makes probabilities, and sampling chooses the next token. Learned parameters total exactly 17,045,504. A block inset explains all 1,774,464 parameters and the GELU nonlinearity.
svg.text: A language model predicts the next piece of text.
Training adjusts these numbers to improve predictions.
Generation reuses them unchanged to continue your text.

g.text: Tokens are pieces of text, each mapped to an integer ID.
A position is its index in the sequence: 0, 1, 2, …
A vector is a list of numbers. An embedding is a learned
vector looked up for a token or a position.
Adding position vectors gives the model a sense of order.
Now 384 numbers flow forward per position.
The stored table entries are learned parameters.
The flowing vectors are activations: values computed
from this input, not newly learned weights.
Each also has layer norms and residual connections.
Same structure; different learned weights in each block.
Attention uses current and earlier positions, never future
tokens. The MLP transforms each position independently,
using the same weights at every position.
3 / TURN THE LAST VECTOR INTO A NEXT-TOKEN GUESS
Normalises feature values within each token vector,
then scales and shifts them. It does not mix positions.
That is a shape, not the number of learned parameters.
18.50% · Untied: it does not reuse the input table.
Temperature adjusts randomness by rescaling scores (logits).
Softmax makes probabilities summing to 1 at each position.
Use the last position’s chances to choose the next token.
Append and repeat; no learned parameters in these steps.
OPEN ONE BLOCK / THE ORDER OF OPERATIONS
Same 384-number input and output width at each position.
1 Normalise, apply attention, add the incoming vector.
2 Normalise, apply MLP, add that stage’s incoming vector.
Adding back the input is a residual (skip) connection.
PARAMETER INVENTORY FOR THOSE TWO STAGES
Two linear layers, with GELU between them.
GELU adds a smooth bend: this can learn nonlinear
patterns instead of collapsing into one linear map.
One before attention; one before the MLP.
Weights are reused; longer context adds no block weights.
GELU and residual additions add no learned parameters.
Boxes show structure, not proportional parameter areas.
